purpose: Define the michi output/error integration boundary for monokl: the exact Cargo.toml dependency shape for adopting the sibling crate michi (github.com/orin-dx/michi, an AGPL-3.0-or-later, agent-facing output/error/truncation primitives library shared across the orin-dx suite), and the exact Rust trait/adapter design that converts monokl's own already-gated domain types (MonoklError from SPEC-001; CodeBlock/RankedBlock from SPEC-006; SearchResponse/SymbolsResult/DependentsResult from SPEC-007) into michi's rendering types (DomainError, AgentResponse, Value) at a single, narrow boundary -- without modifying any of those already-gated types themselves. This track exists because a deep architectural-fit analysis (conducted this session, empirically verified against michi at commit cb355b8c05048e71e7219af8416c475346b6f837 -- this track's pinned rev, per AC-015; the v0.1.0 tag is 68 commits stale and lacks several APIs this track depends on -- not its documentation) found that a naive, direct-coupling integration would either lose information (MonoklError's 14 variants vs. DomainError's 9 fixed ErrorCode values; the retry-by-default semantics on 4 of those codes, which would incorrectly mark monokl's synchronous, local, non-retryable errors as agent-retryable unless explicitly overridden) or actively corrupt data (michi-toon's escape_value function deletes newline characters rather than escaping them -- verified by constructing a real multi-line TypeScript function and observing the rendered TOON cell fold the entire function body into what reads as a single-line comment; toon::list()'s column set is derived from the first row's serialized keys alone, silently dropping or reordering columns when later rows have different populated Option/Vec fields than the first, which lands directly on CodeBlock's and SymbolEntry's already-gated skip_serializing_if fields). This track locks a compile-time-safe adapter (a const-generic ToonProjection<N> trait encoding row arity in the type, eliminating michi-toon's own debug_assert!-based arity panic as a reachable failure mode from monokl's side) and an information-preserving error adapter (a ToDomainError trait carrying monokl's own finer-grained classification as a message prefix, plus explicit error-chain flattening into hints, since DomainError itself implements std::error::Error with an empty body and therefore never exposes source()).
scope: The exact Cargo.toml change adding michi as an optional, git-rev-pinned (not registry, not a tag) dependency gated behind the existing cli feature, plus the cli feature's own feature-list edit; a new output::agent submodule (crates/monokl/src/output/agent.rs, part of the already-declared #[cfg(feature = "cli")] pub mod output; from SPEC-004) containing: the ToDomainError trait and its impl for MonoklError, covering all 14 variants with an explicit ErrorCode mapping, a monokl_code() message-prefix scheme preserving finer-grained classification than michi's 9 fixed codes support, unconditional .retryable(false) (since nothing monokl does locally and synchronously is legitimately agent-retryable), and explicit std::error::Error source-chain flattening into DomainError's hints (since DomainError's own Display/render omit #[source] entirely); the ToonProjection<N> const-generic trait (N encoding row arity as a compile-time guarantee, not a runtime debug_assert!) and its impl for SymbolsResult (9 columns: file plus SymbolEntry's 8 fields) and SearchResponse (7 locator columns -- file, lineStart, lineEnd, nodeKind, symbolSignature, rank, finalScore -- deliberately excluding CodeBlock.code, matched_lines, and matched_keywords from the TOON row entirely, per this track's own resolved design decision, not left open); the cell()/opt_cell() helper functions that pre-escape newline characters before handing a string to michi (since michi-toon's own escape_value deletes them rather than escaping them, and this deletion is unconditional -- the adapter must intercept before the string ever reaches michi, not rely on michi to handle it safely); and three resolved integration-boundary design decisions (a future TOON output mode -- not yet reachable from any CLI surface, since it requires Track 21 to add OutputFormat::Toon first, per non_goals -- must be mutually exclusive with monokl's existing --only/--fields dynamic projection at the clap parsing level, not silently ignored or combined; once reachable, search's TOON output is locator-only, never carrying the code field inline, with a hint pointing callers at the existing extract command for full content; michi remains entirely behind the cli feature gate, including for budget.rs's list-capping logic, which stays michi-free -- budget.rs is compiled unconditionally per SPEC-004's lib.rs, with no cli gate, so an unconditional michi-truncate dependency would be required to use it there, and this track does not adopt that path).
non_goals: output.rs's own presentation-resolution engine (ResolvedProfile/ResolvedFormat/Presentation/resolve_presentation(), per-command text renderers, ANSI color helpers) -- a separate, larger, not-yet-drafted track (ACTIVE.md's Track 21, CLI/pipeline/main.rs). This track locks only the michi-facing adapter submodule (output::agent), not output.rs's broader design.

projection.rs's existing field-aliasing/--format minimal pruning logic -- unaffected by this track; TOON output and monokl's own dynamic JSON projection are two separate, non-overlapping output modes per this track's own resolved design decision (declared mutually exclusive at the CLI level, not merged or reconciled into one system).

budget.rs's token/byte/result-count capping logic and its own truncation-marker string generation (already spec-only, not yet drafted as its own track) -- this track explicitly does not adopt michi-truncate for that logic; michi-truncate's char-count model doesn't fit a token-budget concern regardless, and budget.rs's own always-compiled (non-cli-gated) status means adopting michi there would require an unconditional dependency, which this track deliberately declines.

io-errors' own crate (crates/io-errors, referenced by MonoklError's Io variant via SPEC-001's already-gated #[from] FileIoError) -- a separate, not-yet-implemented crate; this track's error adapter treats MonoklError::Io(FileIoError) as an opaque, already-typed variant to convert, and does not touch FileIoError's own definition or io-errors' own Cargo.toml.

Whether michi's own ErrorCode enum should gain new variants (e.g. a distinct Internal code) to better fit monokl's error shapes -- explicitly considered and explicitly declined for this track: michi's own PRINCIPLES.md gate 3 requires evidence that multiple independent tools need a pattern before it belongs in michi, and monokl's needs alone are one data point, not proof. This track's adapter (the monokl_code() prefix plus explicit .retryable(false)) fully discharges monokl's own needs without requiring a michi-side change.

Whether michi-core's DomainError-from-thiserror-chain conversion helper, or michi-truncate's TruncationOutcome<T>/truncate_by_bytes pattern (already sketched in michi's own PRINCIPLES.md but not yet implemented), should be built inside michi itself -- these are candidate michi-side enhancements, tracked separately (see .claude/plans/MICHI-ADJUSTMENTS.md), not part of what this track locks inside monokl's own repository.

MCP CallToolResult assembly beyond what DomainError::to_call_tool_result() and AgentResponse::to_call_tool_result() already provide -- this track locks the conversion INTO michi's types, not any monokl-specific MCP server logic, which does not yet exist anywhere in this project's spec corpus.

The actual clap Arg wiring that makes a TOON output mode mutually exclusive with monokl's existing --only/--fields flags -- this track resolves the DESIGN DECISION (a TOON output mode must be mutually exclusive with dynamic field selection at parse time, not silently combined or resolved by one overriding the other, because TOON's column set is fixed per ToonProjection<N> implementation (AC-004/AC-005/AC-006) while --only/--fields' whole purpose is dynamic, caller-chosen field selection over monokl's full JSON shape -- combining them would require either abandoning ToonProjection<N>'s compile-time arity guarantee for a runtime-sized alternative, or silently ignoring caller-supplied field selection) but does not implement the clap wiring itself, and does not assume a --format toon flag already exists anywhere. Verified directly: no cli.rs, main.rs, or clap wiring exists in the codebase yet (crates/monokl/src/ contains only lib.rs; crates/monokl/Cargo.toml declares a [[bin]] pointing at src/main.rs, but that file does not exist). The spec corpus, however, DOES sketch a CLI verbatim in two places -- an earlier revision at docs/spec/01-core-architecture.md Section 21 (cli.rs/output.rs, starting :2334) and Section 22 (main.rs, starting :2443), and a later, richer revision at docs/spec/03-multi-language-platform.md:2142-2180 -- but no track has gated either as a spec@1, and neither is code yet; the earlier claim that no clap Arg definitions or Format enum exist anywhere in the spec corpus was false and has been corrected here. Critically, the corpus's own OutputFormat enum (03-multi-language-platform.md:2177: `pub enum OutputFormat { Auto, Json, Minimal, Text, Mermaid, Schema }`, wired at :2153-2156 as a global `--format` ValueEnum arg (doc comment :2153-2154, the #[arg(...)] attribute :2155, the field itself :2156)) has NO Toon variant -- `--format toon` exists in no source document today. Track 21, when drafted, MUST add a new OutputFormat::Toon variant (this exact name, so `--format toon` is its ValueEnum-derived CLI spelling) before this track's adapter is reachable from any CLI surface at all -- this track's own module compiles and is independently testable without that variant existing, since its public functions (ToDomainError, ToonProjection<N>, render_projection, AC-004B) take already-constructed MonoklError/SymbolsResult/SearchResponse values directly, not CLI args or a parsed Cli struct; nothing calls this module from a CLI entry point until Track 21 adds the variant and wires a match arm to it. Track 21 MUST ALSO enforce the mutual-exclusivity constraint above via clap's #[arg(conflicts_with = "...")] attribute (or the equivalent builder-API .conflicts_with() call) once it adds that variant, naming --only and --fields as the conflicting arguments, rejecting the combination with a parse-time error naming both flags before any command logic runs -- an explicit, discoverable CLI error, not a silently-narrowed or silently-ignored flag combination. This track does not resolve which of the corpus's several evolving CLI sketches is canonical, or the exact final per-subcommand flag set: 03-multi-language-platform.md:2351-2360's own "New flags relative to Phase 1.5" delta list shows --only already present on Search (:2354), Inspect (:2357), and Patterns (:2358), and --fields present on Inspect specifically (:2357), as of that document's own Phase-2+ snapshot -- but that same list does not confirm or rule out --fields ever extending to Search or Symbols, and the corpus is not internally definitive on this point. That determination, and reconciling this constraint against whatever CLI surface Track 21 actually locks, belongs to Track 21, not this track. This constraint binds Track 21's future design; it is not left open for reconsideration there.

api_surface.name: ToDomainError::to_domain_error
api_surface.description: crates/monokl/src/output/agent.rs. Implemented for MonoklError. Converts a MonoklError reference into a michi::DomainError, preserving classification (via a monokl_code() message prefix, since michi's 9-value ErrorCode cannot represent all 14 MonoklError variants distinctly) and the full std::error::Error source chain (via explicit chain-walking into DomainError's hints, since DomainError itself never exposes source()). Always sets retryable(false). See AC-005 through AC-011 for the full per-variant mapping.

api_surface.name: ToDomainError::monokl_code
api_surface.description: crates/monokl/src/output/agent.rs. Returns a stable, snake_case discriminator finer-grained than michi's ErrorCode -- one distinct value per MonoklError variant (14 total), e.g. "lock_poisoned", "too_many_terms". Prepended to DomainError.message so it survives every michi render path (render(), render_json(), render_github_annotation(), Display) even though those paths never read this trait directly.

api_surface.name: ToonProjection::toon_rows
api_surface.description: crates/monokl/src/output/agent.rs. A trait generic over a const usize N (the row's column count, fixed per implementing type), implemented for SymbolsResult (N=9) and SearchResponse (N=7). Producing an array of exactly N elements is a compile-time guarantee -- unlike michi-toon's own render_toon(), which only debug_assert!s on a row/header length mismatch at runtime, an implementation of this trait cannot construct a mismatched row without a compile error.

api_surface.name: cell
api_surface.description: crates/monokl/src/output/agent.rs. The only sanctioned way to convert a &str into a michi::toon::Value inside this module. If s contains '\n' or '\r', replaces them (CR dropped, LF replaced with the two-character literal sequence backslash-n) before handing the result to Value::from -- michi-toon's own escape_value deletes these characters silently rather than escaping them (AC-001), so this function must run first, unconditionally, for every string cell this module produces.

api_surface.name: opt_cell
api_surface.description: crates/monokl/src/output/agent.rs. None maps to Value::Null; Some(s) maps to cell(s). Used for every Option<String>-typed field this module projects into a TOON row (SymbolEntry's signature/owner/trait_impl/kind_detail, CodeBlock's symbol_signature).

api_surface.name: render_projection
api_surface.signature: fn render_projection<const N: usize, T: ToonProjection<N>>(value: &T) -> Result<String, michi::DomainError>
api_surface.description: crates/monokl/src/output/agent.rs. The sole function that converts a ToonProjection<N> implementation into a rendered TOON string -- see AC-004B for its exact steps, each independently verified against michi's real source at the pinned rev. Builds a michi::toon::ToonOptions from value.toon_rows()/T::FIELDS/value.toon_total_count() and calls its validate() explicitly, returning Err(toon_validation_error(&e)) on failure (AC-014) before ever constructing a michi::AgentResponse; on success, builds a michi::AgentResponse via .items()/.hints(value.toon_hints())/.total_count() and returns Ok(resp.render_toon()) -- AgentResponse::render_toon(), not the standalone michi::toon::render_toon() free function, since only the former appends toon_hints() (including AC-006's extract-command hint) to the output.
error_conditions: Returns Err(toon_validation_error(&e)) when the constructed ToonOptions fails validate() -- indicates a bug in this module's own ToonProjection<N> implementation, not a caller input error, per AC-014.

api_surface.name: ErrorContext
api_surface.signature: pub struct ErrorContext<'a> { pub command: &'a str }
api_surface.description: crates/monokl/src/output/agent.rs. New code this track defines, not sourced from michi or any monokl spec. Carries the name of the CLI (sub)command currently executing (e.g. "search", "symbols", "extract") into to_domain_error, so RecoveryHint::new() (AC-012) can name the correct tool for an agent to retry -- michi::RecoveryHint::new(tool: impl Into<String>) requires a tool name, and ErrorContext.command supplies it. This module treats command as an opaque, caller-supplied &str -- it does not enumerate or validate it against a fixed set of command names, since the canonical list of monokl's CLI (sub)command names belongs to the not-yet-drafted CLI track (Track 21, per this track's own non_goals), not this adapter.

api_surface.name: symbol_kind_str
api_surface.description: crates/monokl/src/output/agent.rs. New code this track defines: SymbolKind (SPEC-003 AC-001) has no as_str() or Display method of its own -- its full derive list is #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)] plus #[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")] (SPEC-003 AC-001), not merely #[derive(Serialize)] -- this module needs the same camelCase string form for a TOON cell without round-tripping through serde_json. Returns exactly the 15 camelCase forms SPEC-003 AC-002 already locks for serde's own rename_all output (Function->"function" through Other->"other"), via a direct match over all 15 variants with no default/fallback arm -- so this function cannot silently return a wrong string if SymbolKind ever gains a 16th variant; it fails to compile instead, per Rust's exhaustiveness check on a non-#[non_exhaustive] enum (SPEC-003 AC-001 confirms SymbolKind carries no #[non_exhaustive]).

api_surface.name: visibility_str
api_surface.description: crates/monokl/src/output/agent.rs. New code this track defines, for the identical reason as symbol_kind_str: Visibility (SPEC-003 AC-003) has no as_str() or Display method of its own. Returns exactly the 4 camelCase forms SPEC-003 AC-003 already locks (Public->"public", Crate->"crate", Module->"module", Private->"private"), via a direct, exhaustive match over all 4 variants with no default/fallback arm.

api_surface.name: toon_validation_error
api_surface.description: crates/monokl/src/output/agent.rs. Constructs a DomainError directly from a michi::toon::ToonError -- deliberately NOT via the ToDomainError trait, which is scoped only to MonoklError's closed 14-value monokl_code() set (AC-007). Used when this module's own explicit ToonOptions::validate() call (AC-014) fails, indicating a bug in this module's own row/field construction, not a caller input error. Always sets retryable(false).

api_surface.name: innermost_walk_error
api_surface.description: crates/monokl/src/output/agent.rs. Recursively unwraps ignore::Error's own public WithLineNumber/WithPath/WithDepth wrapper variants and single-element Partial(vec![e]) down to a leaf variant -- see AC-009 for the full rationale (ignore::Error never overrides std::error::Error::source(), so a source()-based walk cannot reach a leaf) and the exhaustive leaf-to-ErrorCode match this function's result feeds into. This exact function and its downstream match were compiled and run against the real ignore v0.4.33 crate in an isolated throwaway crate before being locked into this spec, confirming both compile successfully with zero warnings and produce the stated ErrorCode for every one of ignore::Error's 9 variants, including the nested-Glob-inside-WithPath-inside-WithLineNumber shape a real malformed .gitignore line actually produces.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Verified directly against michi at commit cb355b8c05048e71e7219af8416c475346b6f837 (this track's pinned rev, per AC-015), not its documentation: crates/michi-toon/src/escape.rs's character-handling match arms treat '\n' and '\r' as no-ops -- the characters are silently dropped from the output entirely, not escaped into a literal representation. Constructing a real multi-line string (a TypeScript function with a leading `//` comment line followed by a code body on subsequent lines) and passing it through michi-toon's rendering path produces a single TOON cell where every line has been concatenated with no separator, placing the entire function body after the `//` on the first line -- syntactically and semantically corrupting the content, not merely making it harder to read. This holds regardless of any ToonOptions configuration (including max_cell_len); there is no michi-toon configuration that causes newlines to be preserved or escaped rather than deleted.
acceptance_criteria.rationale: This is an empirical claim about a third-party crate's exact runtime behavior, not a design choice this track is making -- it is stated as verified fact (checked against real compiled michi source) precisely because this project's established discipline treats unverified claims about serde/library runtime behavior as the single most common source of error across every prior track's correction history, and this is the first track making claims about a genuinely external crate's behavior rather than monokl's own verbatim-specified source.

acceptance_criteria.criterion:
cell(s: &str) -> michi::toon::Value (01-core-architecture.md has no citation for this function, since it does not exist in monokl's own spec'd source -- this is new code this track designs) checks s for the presence of '
' or ''; if either is present, it constructs a new String with every '' character removed and every '
' character replaced with the two literal ASCII characters backslash and n (i.e. the visible two-character sequence 
, not a control character), then wraps the result via Value::from; if neither is present, s is passed to Value::from unmodified with no allocation beyond what Value::from itself performs. opt_cell(s: Option<&str>) returns Value::Null for None and cell's result for Some(s) -- this is the only place in this module where Value::Null is ever constructed for a genuinely-absent value, as distinct from cell's own handling of an empty string (Some("") maps through cell to a Value containing zero characters, not Value::Null -- the two are distinguishable at the Rust call-site level, though AC-013 notes they are not distinguishable once rendered).

Verified directly against michi at commit cb355b8c05048e71e7219af8416c475346b6f837 (this track's pinned rev, per AC-015): crates/michi-toon/src/lib.rs's list<T: Serialize>(type_name, items) function derives its column set (field names and their order) from the first element in items whose serialized JSON object is non-empty, via the exact guard `if fields.is_empty() && !obj.is_empty() { fields = obj.keys().cloned().collect(); }` -- an element whose own serde_json::to_value happens to produce an empty object (e.g. every field is skipped via skip_serializing_if) does not fix the column set, but a row is still pushed for it at that point using whatever fields currently holds -- a zero-length row, since fields is still empty when this happens. If one or more such empty-object elements precede the first populated element in items, list() ends up with a rows Vec containing at least one zero-length row while fields is eventually fixed to a non-zero length by the later, first-populated element; ToonOptions::validate(), called unconditionally at the end of list() before render_toon() ever runs, iterates rows in order and returns Err(ToonError::RowLengthMismatch { row_index, expected: fields.len(), actual: 0 }) for the first such zero-length row's index -- list() therefore returns this Err and renders nothing at all for that call, rather than silently reordering, dropping, or overwriting that row (verified directly: ToonOptions::validate()'s own row-length loop, crates/michi-toon/src/lib.rs, checks `row.len() != self.fields.len()` per row in declaration order and returns on the first mismatch). No element's keys are ever unioned with another's -- once any element has fixed the column set (the first element whose object is non-empty), every subsequent element is rendered against that already-fixed set, whether or not that later element's own object happens to be empty (a later empty-object element renders as an all-null row of the already-fixed length, not a zero-length one, since fields is no longer empty by the time that row is built -- this does not trigger RowLengthMismatch). When T has one or more fields carrying #[serde(skip_serializing_if = "...")] (the pattern SPEC-003 AC-005 -- not AC-006, which addresses SymbolEntry's unrelated deny_unknown_fields absence -- and SPEC-006 AC-002 already establish for SymbolEntry's Option fields and CodeBlock's Vec fields), an element whose skip_serializing_if condition is true for a given field produces a serialized JSON object missing that field's key entirely -- if this happens to be the FIRST element in items, that column is absent from every row's rendered output, including later elements where the same field is actually populated; conversely, a different first element yields a different, larger column set. This module therefore never calls michi::toon::list(); every ToonProjection<N> implementation in this module supplies an explicit, fixed FIELDS: [&'static str; N] constant instead, independent of any element's actual serialized shape or of which element happens to be first.
acceptance_criteria.rationale: Verified empirically against real michi source rather than assumed from its public API description, per the same discipline as AC-001 -- this is the second of two verified michi-toon defects this module's design exists specifically to route around.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: The ToonProjection<const N: usize> trait (crates/monokl/src/output/agent.rs, new code) is defined with N as a trait-level const generic parameter, not an associated const, with signature: `pub trait ToonProjection<const N: usize> { const TYPE_NAME: &'static str; const FIELDS: [&'static str; N]; fn toon_rows(&self) -> Vec<[Value; N]>; fn toon_total_count(&self) -> Option<usize> { None }; fn toon_hints(&self) -> Vec<michi::Hint> { Vec::new() }; }`. Because FIELDS is typed [&'static str; N] and toon_rows returns Vec<[Value; N]>, any implementation whose FIELDS array length does not match its toon_rows' per-row array length fails to compile with a fixed-size-array type mismatch -- there is no runtime state in which an implementation of this trait can produce a row whose length disagrees with its own declared header, which is the exact failure class michi-toon's own render_toon() only catches at runtime -- verified directly against michi's real source at the pinned rev (crates/michi-toon/src/render.rs:140-147): `#[cfg(debug_assertions)] for row in rows { debug_assert!(row.len() == field_count, ...); }`, a debug-build-only check distinct from both AC-001's escape_value newline-deletion finding and AC-003's list()-column-derivation finding -- neither of which addresses render_toon()'s arity check, so this fact is stated and cited here directly rather than attributed to either.

render_projection<const N: usize, T: ToonProjection<N>>(value: &T) -> Result<String, michi::DomainError> is the sole function in this module that turns a ToonProjection<N> implementation into a rendered TOON string; no other criterion or api_surface entry in this spec defines this conversion, and AC-006's toon_hints() extract-command hint and AC-004's toon_total_count() default are consumed only through this function. Its exact steps, each verified against michi's real source at the pinned rev (AC-015): (1) `let rows: Vec<Vec<Value>> = value.toon_rows().into_iter().map(|row| row.to_vec()).collect();` and `let fields: Vec<String> = T::FIELDS.iter().map(|s| (*s).to_string()).collect();` (michi::toon::ToonOptions::new's second parameter is Vec<String>, not &[&str] -- verified: `pub fn new(type_name: impl Into<String>, fields: Vec<String>, rows: Vec<Vec<Value>>) -> Self`, crates/michi-toon/src/lib.rs, so T::FIELDS's [&'static str; N] must be converted; michi::AgentResponse::items's fields parameter is the different type &[&str], so T::FIELDS.as_slice() is used there directly with no conversion, per step (3)). (2) `let opts = michi::toon::ToonOptions::new(T::TYPE_NAME, fields, rows.clone()).total_count(value.toon_total_count());` -- ToonOptions::total_count takes Option<usize> directly (verified: `pub fn total_count(mut self, total: Option<usize>) -> Self`), matching toon_total_count()'s own return type with no Some/None branching needed at this step. Then `if let Err(e) = opts.validate() { return Err(toon_validation_error(&e)); }` -- this is the explicit, caller-side validate() call AC-014 requires, performed before any michi::AgentResponse is constructed. (3) On Ok, `let mut resp = michi::AgentResponse::new(T::TYPE_NAME).items(rows, T::FIELDS.as_slice()).hints(value.toon_hints());` (verified: `pub fn items(mut self, rows: Vec<Vec<Value>>, fields: &[&str]) -> Self` moves rows by value, consuming the original -- the rows.clone() in step (1)/(2) exists specifically so this step still has an owned Vec<Vec<Value>> to move, since step (2)'s ToonOptions already consumed a clone for validation; `pub fn hints(mut self, hints: Vec<Hint>) -> Self` accepts AC-004's toon_hints() return type, Vec<michi::Hint>, directly with no conversion). (4) `if let Some(n) = value.toon_total_count() { resp = resp.total_count(n); }` -- michi::AgentResponse::total_count takes a plain usize, not Option<usize> (verified: `pub fn total_count(mut self, n: usize) -> Self`), unlike ToonOptions's own same-named method in step (2) -- the two total_count methods on two different builders have different signatures, so this step's Option-unwrapping guard is required and is not interchangeable with step (2)'s direct pass-through. (5) `Ok(resp.render_toon())` -- michi::AgentResponse::render_toon(&self) -> String is a real, existing public method (verified: crates/michi-core/src/response.rs, `pub fn render_toon(&self) -> String { self.finish_text(&self.toon_body()) }`), not a free function this module must reimplement; finish_text appends self.hints (the Vec<Hint> attached in step (3)) via the same help[N]:-block mechanism AC-010 already establishes for DomainError, so toon_hints()'s content -- including AC-006's extract-command hint -- reaches the final output through this call, not through michi::toon::render_toon(&opts) (the free function on ToonOptions, which does render ToonOptions.hints -- a Vec<String> field, verified: render_toon(opts) calls render::render(..., &opts.hints, ...), which does emit a help[N]: block for it -- but step (2) of this function never calls .hints(...) on the ToonOptions it builds, so that field stays empty regardless; separately, toon_hints() returns Vec<michi::Hint>, a different type than ToonOptions::hints()'s Vec<String> parameter, and is attached to the AgentResponse instead, where AgentResponse::hints(Vec<Hint>) accepts it directly with no conversion -- so AgentResponse::render_toon() is not preferred because the free function cannot append hints at all, but because this function's own design routes toon_hints() through the AgentResponse builder specifically, and the free function's parallel ToonOptions.hints mechanism is simply never populated here).
acceptance_criteria.rationale: This function's existence and exact shape is new design work this track adds, not sourced from any single spec citation -- discovered as a genuine gap during this track's own gating: no prior draft of this spec ever named the function that consumes ToonProjection<N> and produces a string, even though AC-006 already required a toon_hints()-carried extract hint to reach rendered output somehow. The design was corrected mid-gating from an earlier, incorrect sketch that called michi::toon::render_toon(&opts) directly on a standalone ToonOptions (which would have silently dropped every hint, defeating AC-006's own requirement) -- resolved instead by routing through michi::AgentResponse's real builder and its real, existing render_toon() method, which does append hints, verified directly against michi-core/src/response.rs rather than assumed from AgentResponse's other, better-known methods (to_call_tool_result(), render_json()).

acceptance_criteria.criterion: impl ToonProjection<9> for SymbolsResult projects each (file, SymbolEntry) pair across SymbolsResult.files (a BTreeMap<Utf8PathBuf, Vec<SymbolEntry>>, SPEC-007 AC-013) into one row of 9 columns, in this exact order: file (the BTreeMap key, via cell(f.as_str()) -- Utf8PathBuf::as_str() is a real, already-existing camino method, unlike SymbolKind/Visibility below), name (cell), kind (cell(symbol_kind_str(e.kind)) -- SymbolKind (SPEC-003 AC-001) has no as_str() or Display method of its own, so this module's own symbol_kind_str() helper supplies the camelCase string form instead), line (Value::from(e.line), a plain usize -- not run through cell, since usize cannot contain a newline), signature (opt_cell(e.signature.as_deref())), owner (opt_cell(e.owner.as_deref())), traitImpl (opt_cell(e.trait_impl.as_deref())), visibility (opt_cell(e.visibility.map(visibility_str)) -- Visibility (SPEC-003 AC-003) likewise has no as_str() of its own, so this module's own visibility_str() helper supplies it), kindDetail (opt_cell(e.kind_detail.as_deref())). This is 9 columns, not the 8 an earlier, less careful pass at this design mistakenly used (omitting kindDetail) -- SymbolEntry has exactly 8 fields per SPEC-003 AC-004 (name/kind/line/signature/owner/trait_impl/visibility/kind_detail), and this projection's own file column is a 9th, added by the flattening operation itself, not one of SymbolEntry's own fields. TYPE_NAME is "symbols". FIELDS is exactly ["file","name","kind","line","signature","owner","traitImpl","visibility","kindDetail"], in this order, matching the row order exactly.
acceptance_criteria.rationale: This is new design work, not a verbatim lock of pre-specified source -- the exact column set and order is a genuine choice this track makes, informed by SymbolEntry's already-gated field list but not dictated by any single source citation, so it is flagged as a judgment call rather than presented as though it were extracted from an existing document.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: impl ToonProjection<7> for SearchResponse projects each RankedBlock in SearchResponse.results (SPEC-007 AC-011, SPEC-006 AC-005) into one row of 7 columns, in this exact order: file (cell(block.block.file.as_str())), lineStart (Value::from(block.block.line_start)), lineEnd (Value::from(block.block.line_end)), nodeKind (cell(symbol_kind_str(block.block.node_kind))), symbolSignature (opt_cell(block.block.symbol_signature.as_deref())), rank (Value::from(block.rank)), finalScore (Value::from(block.final_score)) -- where the outer binding block: &RankedBlock is the loop variable name and block.block is RankedBlock's own field of that same name holding a CodeBlock (SPEC-006 AC-005: `block: CodeBlock` is RankedBlock's first field). #[serde(flatten)] on that field (SPEC-006 AC-005/AC-006) is a serialize-time-only directive that merges CodeBlock's JSON keys into RankedBlock's own output object; it does not change Rust struct field access, which still requires naming the field (block.block.file, not block.file) -- file/lineStart/lineEnd/nodeKind/symbolSignature therefore all resolve through block.block (CodeBlock's own fields, per SPEC-006 AC-001), while rank/finalScore resolve directly off block (two of RankedBlock's own 6 fields, per SPEC-006 AC-005, not CodeBlock's), and nodeKind uses this module's own symbol_kind_str() helper for the same reason AC-005's kind column does (SymbolKind has no as_str() of its own). This deliberately excludes CodeBlock.code, CodeBlock.matched_lines, and CodeBlock.matched_keywords from the TOON row entirely -- code is potentially multi-line (AC-001's corruption risk, which cell()'s newline substitution would prevent from corrupting the row but would still produce one extremely long, barely-scannable cell defeating TOON's own purpose as a cheap, scannable overview format), and matched_lines/matched_keywords are collections that michi-toon has no native representation for beyond JSON-stringifying into a single cell (also defeating the scannable-overview purpose). This projection also excludes RankedBlock's own bm25_score/coverage_boost/node_type_boost (the three component signals combining into final_score, which IS included) and parent_context: Option<ParentContext> -- both exclusions are deliberate, not oversights: final_score alone is sufficient for a caller deciding whether a row is worth following up on via extract, and the full component breakdown plus enclosing ParentContext remain available via the existing, unaffected JSON output path (--format json, no flag change) for any caller that needs them; a locator table's value is in staying small and scannable, not in reproducing every field JSON already carries. TYPE_NAME is "search". FIELDS is exactly ["file","lineStart","lineEnd","nodeKind","symbolSignature","rank","finalScore"], in this order. toon_hints() includes a hint whose text names the extract command and its file/lineStart/lineEnd parameters -- the camelCase, agent-facing JSON spelling this hint uses for readability, not ExtractRequest's own Rust field names, which are file/line_start/line_end (ExtractRequest, SPEC-008 AC-007) -- as the mechanism for retrieving a given row's actual code content -- this projection is a locator table, not a content-carrying one, and the hint makes that discoverable rather than silent.
acceptance_criteria.rationale: This is the resolved version of an open design question the preceding architectural-fit research explicitly left unresolved (locator-only vs. inline-newline-escaped code). Resolved here in favor of locator-only: TOON's own value proposition (cheap, scannable, token-efficient) is actively undermined by embedding a multi-line code block as a single long escaped cell even once corruption is prevented, and monokl already has a dedicated, already-gated command (extract, SPEC-008) for retrieving full code content by location -- making locator-plus-extract a textbook progressive-disclosure pattern rather than an arbitrary restriction.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: monokl_code(&self) -> &'static str, implemented for MonoklError, returns exactly one of these 14 distinct snake_case strings, one per variant, matching variant declaration order (SPEC-001 AC-001): "io", "walk", "regex_build", "non_utf8_path", "too_many_terms", "tokenizer_init", "json", "path_outside_root", "stale_disk_cache", "invalid_git_ref", "git", "symlink_rejected", "file_too_large", "lock_poisoned". No two variants share a monokl_code() value, and no variant returns an empty string or a string containing whitespace.

to_domain_error(&self, ctx: ErrorContext<'_>) -> michi::DomainError, implemented for MonoklError. ErrorContext<'a> is new code this track defines (not sourced from michi or any monokl spec): `pub struct ErrorContext<'a> { pub command: &'a str }`, carrying the name of the CLI (sub)command currently executing (e.g. "search", "symbols", "extract"), needed because RecoveryHint::new() (AC-012) requires a tool name and this module treats command as an opaque, caller-supplied &str -- it is not enumerated or validated against a fixed command-name set here, since that canonical list belongs to the not-yet-drafted CLI track (Track 21, per this track's own non_goals). to_domain_error maps each of the 14 MonoklError variants to exactly one michi::ErrorCode as follows: RegexBuild, NonUtf8Path, TooManyTerms, InvalidGitRef, FileTooLarge -> ErrorCode::InvalidInput (all five represent a caller-supplied or caller-triggered input condition monokl rejects, not an internal failure or an external dependency's fault); PathOutsideRoot, SymlinkRejected -> ErrorCode::Forbidden (both are safety-boundary refusals of an otherwise-well-formed request); StaleDiskCache -> ErrorCode::Conflict (a resource-state mismatch, matching ErrorCode::Conflict's own doc comment, "Resource state mismatch." -- with AC-011's unconditional .retryable(false) applied on top, this still classifies as ErrorClass::User via ErrorCode::Conflict.default_class(), not ErrorClass::Internal); TokenizerInit, Json, Git, LockPoisoned -> ErrorCode::ExternalFailure (four variants with no closer-fitting code among michi's fixed 9 -- TokenizerInit and LockPoisoned are internal-invariant-violation shaped rather than genuinely "a downstream dependency failed" shaped, a mismatch this criterion does not resolve at the ErrorCode level, per non_goals; the monokl_code() prefix (AC-007) is what actually distinguishes them for an agent reading the message); Io, Walk -> a fan-out, not a fixed code, since both variants wrap a std::io::Error-bearing sub-error whose io::ErrorKind determines the outcome, per AC-009.
acceptance_criteria.rationale: The ErrorCode assignment for the four ExternalFailure-mapped variants (TokenizerInit, Json, Git, LockPoisoned) is a deliberate best-fit choice among michi's fixed 9 values, not a claim that ExternalFailure is semantically accurate for TokenizerInit or LockPoisoned specifically -- LockPoisoned's own Display text (SPEC-001 AC-018) states outright that it represents an internal bug, not an external dependency failure, and this criterion does not paper over that mismatch; it states the mapping precisely and defers the finer-grained distinction to monokl_code().

acceptance_criteria.criterion: For MonoklError::Io(FileIoError), to_domain_error inspects the wrapped error's underlying std::io::Error (accessed via FileIoError::io_source() (docs/spec/01-core-architecture.md:3005-3013, Section 27's verbatim io-errors source -- a #[must_use] pub fn io_source(&self) -> &io::Error method returning the wrapped io::Error directly, one of FileIoError's own already-specified accessor methods, not an invented API)) and its .kind(): io::ErrorKind::NotFound maps to ErrorCode::NotFound; io::ErrorKind::PermissionDenied maps to ErrorCode::Forbidden; any other io::ErrorKind maps to ErrorCode::ExternalFailure. For MonoklError::Walk { source: ignore::Error, .. }, to_domain_error does NOT walk source via std::error::Error::source() -- verified directly against ignore's real source (checked across every locally cached 0.4.x release, 0.4.18 through 0.4.33; the variant set and field shapes are byte-identical across all of them): `impl std::error::Error for Error` overrides only the deprecated description() method and never overrides source(), so source() returns None unconditionally for every one of ignore::Error's 9 variants -- the string "fn source" appears zero times in ignore's own src/lib.rs, in any cached version. A source-chain walk over source as a &dyn std::error::Error would therefore terminate immediately with None, never reaching a resolvable io::ErrorKind. Instead, this module recursively unwraps ignore::Error's own public WithLineNumber { err: Box<Error>, .. }, WithPath { err: Box<Error>, .. }, and WithDepth { err: Box<Error>, .. } variants, and single-element Partial(vec![e]), down to a leaf, via: `fn innermost_walk_error(e: &ignore::Error) -> &ignore::Error { match e { ignore::Error::WithLineNumber { err, .. } => innermost_walk_error(err), ignore::Error::WithPath { err, .. } => innermost_walk_error(err), ignore::Error::WithDepth { err, .. } => innermost_walk_error(err), ignore::Error::Partial(errs) if errs.len() == 1 => innermost_walk_error(&errs[0]), other => other } }` (see api_surface). The result then feeds a match covering all 9 of ignore::Error's variants explicitly, with no wildcard arm and no match guard anywhere (ignore::Error carries no #[non_exhaustive]; this exact function, including this exact match, was compiled and run against the real ignore v0.4.33 crate -- the version `ignore = "0.4"` currently resolves to -- in an isolated throwaway crate, with zero warnings and zero errors, before being locked here): `match leaf { ignore::Error::Io(io_err) => <the io::ErrorKind fan-out above>, ignore::Error::Glob { .. } => ErrorCode::InvalidInput, ignore::Error::Loop { .. } => ErrorCode::ExternalFailure, ignore::Error::UnrecognizedFileType(_) => ErrorCode::InvalidInput, ignore::Error::InvalidDefinition => ErrorCode::InvalidInput, ignore::Error::Partial(errs) => { let _ = errs; ErrorCode::ExternalFailure }, ignore::Error::WithLineNumber { .. } => unreachable!(...), ignore::Error::WithPath { .. } => unreachable!(...), ignore::Error::WithDepth { .. } => unreachable!(...) }`. The Partial arm is deliberately unguarded (a guarded arm, e.g. `Partial(errs) if errs.len() != 1`, does not satisfy rustc's exhaustiveness checker even alongside other arms covering the same variant, since match guards are ignored for exhaustiveness purposes -- confirmed by compiling both forms) -- it accepts any Vec<Error> unconditionally, since by the time control reaches this match, innermost_walk_error has already recursed into and consumed every Partial whose length is exactly 1, so a Partial reaching this arm is, by construction, never length 1, without needing an internal length check to say so; the three wrapper-variant arms (WithLineNumber/WithPath/WithDepth) are unreachable for the same reason -- innermost_walk_error's own recursion strips them before returning -- and exist in this match only because rustc requires every variant of a non-#[non_exhaustive] enum to be named when no wildcard arm is present; unreachable!() is the correct body for them, not an ErrorCode, since reaching one at runtime would indicate a bug in innermost_walk_error itself, not a real classification to make. Glob maps to InvalidInput (a malformed ignore-pattern in a .gitignore-style file) -- this is the common shape for a walk-time pattern failure, not an edge case: ignore's own gitignore parser wraps a per-line Glob failure in WithLineNumber and then WithPath context via a private, ignore-internal helper (not called by this module directly -- monokl only ever receives the already-wrapped result) before returning it (add_line itself just returns the bare error; it is add(), gitignore.rs's per-line driver, that catches add_line's Err and wraps it via err.tagged(path, lineno) before accumulating it), so `WithPath { err: WithLineNumber { err: Glob { .. }, .. }, .. }` -- a nested Glob, not a bare top-level one -- is the shape a real malformed-gitignore-line failure actually takes; matching only a bare, unwrapped Glob variant, as an earlier draft of this criterion did, would miss this case entirely (independently reproduced: constructing this exact nested shape and running it through classify() in the same compiled probe above correctly yields ErrorCode::InvalidInput, not the unreachable!() arm). Loop maps to ExternalFailure (a symlink cycle detected during traversal -- a filesystem-state condition, not a caller-input-shaped failure the way Glob is, and no closer-fitting code exists among michi's fixed 9, matching AC-008's own established pattern for variants with no closer fit); UnrecognizedFileType maps to InvalidInput (an unrecognized --type filter value the caller supplied); InvalidDefinition maps to InvalidInput (a caller-supplied custom file-type definition that failed to parse); a Partial reaching this match (necessarily length 0 or 2+, per above) maps to ExternalFailure (no single leaf error to attribute this to unambiguously). monokl_code() remains "io" or "walk" respectively regardless of which ErrorCode the fan-out selects -- the prefix identifies the MonoklError variant, not the resolved ErrorCode.
acceptance_criteria.rationale: The Walk-side fan-out mechanism this criterion originally specified (a std::error::Error::source() walk over ignore::Error) does not work -- verified empirically this round that ignore::Error never overrides source(), the same discipline this track has applied to every other empirical claim about an external crate. The replacement mechanism (a hand-written recursive unwrap of ignore::Error's own public wrapper variants, then an exhaustive match on the leaf) is new design work, not sourced from any monokl document: ignore does appear in docs/spec/*.md -- at ten locations across three files, all either dependency declarations (01-core-architecture.md:98, :3072) or ignore::WalkBuilder/WalkParallel traversal usages (01-core-architecture.md:986, :2205, :2298; 02-inspection-and-analysis.md:752, :1029; 03-multi-language-platform.md:331, :2024), plus the source: ignore::Error field declaration this criterion exists to classify (01-core-architecture.md:207) -- but none of the ten specifies or implies anything about how to classify ignore::Error's own variants, which is genuinely new work this track originates -- the ErrorCode assignments for Loop/UnrecognizedFileType/InvalidDefinition/multi-element-Partial are this track's own judgment calls, following AC-008's own established pattern (best-fit among michi's fixed 9, no closer-fitting code required to exist) rather than a locked-elsewhere fact.

acceptance_criteria.criterion:
to_domain_error constructs DomainError::new(code, format!("{}: {head}", self.monokl_code())) where head is the first line of self's own thiserror-generated Display text (self.to_string(), respecting whichever #[error(...)] format each of the 14 variants locks -- the individual Display literals are locked one criterion per variant at SPEC-001 AC-004 through AC-018 and AC-020, not at AC-001, which locks only variant declaration order and field shapes; including Io's #[error(transparent)] marker, which AC-001 does state directly and AC-004 restates in full, where this is identical to the wrapped FileIoError's own Display, per thiserror's documented transparent behavior). Every line after head comes from a separate chain-flattening walk that starts at self.source() -- not at self, which head already covers -- and continues through that error's own .source(), and so on until None; this ordering matters: head is always computed from self's own Display, never from self.source()'s -- an implementation that instead treated self.source()'s Display as head, skipping self's own message entirely, would be a different and incorrect reading this criterion rules out: for Walk { path, #[source] source: ignore::Error }, self.source() yields only the wrapped ignore::Error's own message, never the path field, which exists solely in Walk's own Display text; for Json(#[from] serde_json::Error) (not #[error(transparent)], unlike Io), self's own Display is instead a fixed literal carrying no interpolated field at all -- exactly "json parsing or serialization failed" per SPEC-001 AC-011's correction to the literal at 01-core-architecture.md:222 -- so that text exists only in self's own Display and is entirely absent from self.source()'s Display, which yields the wrapped serde_json::Error's own message alone, with no trace of monokl's own fixed framing text; so head must always be self's own Display, never self.source()'s, or these two variants (Walk by omitting path, Json by omitting monokl's own framing text entirely) silently lose real information, contradicting this track's own information-preserving purpose. Both head and every line the source-walk produces are joined by first splitting each link's own Display output (self's own Display for head, and every source link's own Display for the walk) on any of the three line-boundary forms -- '
' (checked first, consuming both characters as one boundary, never leaving a dangling '
' to also match the standalone-'
' rule), standalone '
', or standalone '' (a bare carriage return with no following '
', which some subprocess output uses for in-place progress updates) -- before treating each resulting line as a separate entry in the walk -- this is necessary because a single link in the chain (e.g. MonoklError::Git's message field -- built from gix's own error Display text, not a git subprocess's stderr: monokl uses gix, a native Rust git implementation, and git_scope.rs's own construction sites format! this field directly from a gix error value, e.g. format!("{base} {head}: {err}") and format!("{git_ref}:{path}: {err}") at 03-multi-language-platform.md:1395-1397 and :1536-1563 -- neither of which shells out to a git binary) can, defensively, itself contain embedded newlines -- no cited construction site is confirmed to actually produce one, but nothing in gix's own Display contract rules it out either, so this module guards against the possibility rather than assuming it away, and DomainError::render() (verified against michi's real source, crates/michi-core/src/error.rs and hints.rs, at the pinned rev per AC-015) writes message as a single raw `message: {text}
` line and writes hints, separately, via append_hints() as a COUNTED block -- `help[{hints.len()}]:
` followed by exactly hints.len() lines, each `  {hint}
` (two-space indented) -- with no newline sanitization applied to either. An un-flattened multi-line message therefore emits extra physical lines carrying no `message:`/`help[`/`  ` prefix at all, indistinguishable from whatever block follows; an un-flattened multi-line hint desynchronizes the count render() already declared in `help[N]:` from the number of physical lines that actually follow it, since N is fixed at hints.len() (the number of Hint values passed in) before any individual hint's own embedded newlines are considered -- a line-oriented parser reading exactly N declared hint lines would read past the intended block into that hint's own later lines, or (for the last hint) into whatever comes after the hints block entirely. Every line after the first (across the whole flattened walk, not just the first link) becomes a separate .hint(line) call on the DomainError builder, in the order the walk produced them. If self has no source() at all (Self::source() returns None, e.g. for TooManyTerms or TokenizerInit, whose thiserror #[error(...)] attributes carry no #[source] field per SPEC-001 AC-001's own field-shape lock), the source-walk that would otherwise start at self.source() produces zero further lines, so no hints are added by this step beyond head itself (though monokl_code()-specific enrichment per AC-012, not this criterion, may still add hints for TooManyTerms specifically).
acceptance_criteria.rationale: This is the resolved fix for a verified information-loss gap: michi's own DomainError has an empty impl std::error::Error for DomainError {} (source() always returns None) and its Display/thiserror derive on the outer michi::Error enum does not include #[source] text either, so a naive DomainError::new(code, self.to_string()) would silently discard every std::error::Error-chained cause -- verified directly against michi's real source, not assumed.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: to_domain_error calls .retryable(false) unconditionally on every constructed DomainError, for all 14 MonoklError variants, regardless of which ErrorCode was selected -- overriding ErrorCode::is_retryable_by_default()'s own default of true for the RateLimited/Unavailable/Timeout/ExternalFailure group, which AC-008 shows 4 of MonoklError's 14 variants map into. This is necessary because michi::Error::class() (verified against michi's real source) checks the DomainError's own retryable field before falling back to ErrorCode::default_class() -- so without this explicit override, TokenizerInit/Json/Git/LockPoisoned would each default to retryable: true and classify as ErrorClass::Transient, incorrectly signaling to an agent that re-issuing an identical monokl invocation might succeed, when monokl is a synchronous, local, filesystem-and-parsing tool with no legitimately transient failure mode among any of its 14 variants -- re-running an identical command against identical on-disk state and code produces the identical error every time.

TooManyTerms { count, limit }, FileTooLarge { path, size, cap }, and InvalidGitRef { ref_, reason } each receive additional enrichment beyond the base to_domain_error path, appended after the chain-flattening hints from AC-010 (which produce none for any of these three, since none carries a #[source] field per SPEC-001 AC-001's own field-shape lock): TooManyTerms gets a .hint(format!("you supplied {count} terms; the limit is {limit}")) call and a .recovery(RecoveryHint::new(ctx.command).param("maxTerms", KvValue::Int(limit as i64)).reason("re-run with a shorter query")) call; FileTooLarge gets a .hint(format!("{path} is {size} bytes; the cap is {cap} bytes")) call and a .recovery(RecoveryHint::new(ctx.command).param("maxBytes", KvValue::Int(cap as i64)).reason("the file exceeds this workspace's size cap")) call; InvalidGitRef gets a .hint(format!("{ref_:?} is not a valid git ref: {reason}")) call with no accompanying .recovery(), since reason is free-form guidance text already, not a parameter an agent could usefully retry with. These three variants were selected because each carries structured numeric or string fields whose values translate directly into concrete, self-contained agent guidance without requiring knowledge of a not-yet-confirmed CLI surface (unlike StaleDiskCache, whose own recovery text -- "run mnkl init --rebuild" -- was deliberately removed from its Display literal per SPEC-001 AC-020's correction, and re-adding equivalent guidance here would require a real mnkl init --rebuild command to exist, which no source document confirms). The remaining 11 variants receive no enrichment beyond AC-010's base chain-flattening in this track; further per-variant enrichment, if warranted, is left for a later track.
acceptance_criteria.rationale: Selecting exactly these three variants for hint/recovery enrichment (rather than all 14, or none) is a deliberate scope-limiting choice: TooManyTerms, FileTooLarge, and InvalidGitRef each carry structured numeric or string fields (count/limit; size/cap; ref_/reason) that translate directly into concrete, self-contained agent guidance without requiring knowledge of a not-yet-confirmed CLI surface. The remaining 11 variants either carry no fields that translate into actionable guidance this cheaply (e.g. LockPoisoned, TokenizerInit -- internal-invariant-violation shaped failures where telling an agent to retry-with-different-parameters makes no sense, since no caller-supplied parameter caused them), or their natural recovery advice depends on a not-yet-confirmed CLI surface the same way StaleDiskCache's removed advice did (SPEC-001 AC-020's correction deliberately stripped 'run mnkl init --rebuild' from that variant's own Display text for exactly this reason -- no source document confirms an init --rebuild command exists). Extending enrichment to any of the 11 would require either inventing recovery guidance not grounded in a real, confirmed command, or adding a hint with no corresponding recovery() call, which this track's own established pattern (AC-010's base chain-flattening, applied uniformly to all 14) already covers adequately without per-variant special-casing. Further per-variant enrichment, if warranted once more of monokl's CLI surface is locked, is left for a later track rather than guessed at here.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Verified directly against michi's real source: michi::toon::Value::Null and michi::toon::Value::from("") (an empty string) render to the identical, indistinguishable empty TOON cell -- there is no way for a reader of rendered TOON output to tell apart a field that was Option::None from a field that was Some(String::new()). Consequently, wherever this module calls opt_cell on a monokl Option<String> field, the rendered output cannot distinguish "this field does not apply to this row" from "this field applies but happens to be an empty string" -- for every field this track projects (SymbolEntry's Option<String> fields signature/owner/trait_impl/kind_detail, plus visibility -- Option<Visibility>, not Option<String>, converted to Option<&str> via visibility_str (AC-005) before reaching opt_cell, at which point the same Value::Null-vs-empty-string ambiguity applies identically -- and CodeBlock's symbol_signature), no source document states that an empty-but-Some value is a meaningful, distinguishable case from None, so this ambiguity is accepted as a property of the TOON output format rather than resolved by this track.
acceptance_criteria.rationale: This is a genuinely unresolved ambiguity inherited from michi's own Value representation, not something this track's own design can close without either abandoning Value::Null (e.g. rendering None as a sentinel string instead, which would itself be a new, undocumented convention) or accepting the ambiguity -- accepting it and stating it precisely is preferred over silently leaving it undiscovered.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Before calling AgentResponse::render_toon() (or any AgentResponse::render() path that reaches the TOON branch) on any ToonOptions this module constructs, this module calls ToonOptions::validate() explicitly and checks its Result itself, rather than relying on AgentResponse's own internal handling. Verified directly against michi's real source: AgentResponse::toon_body() DOES call opts.validate() internally (it is not skipped), but on an Err it returns the string "error: toon_validation_failed\nmessage: {e}\n" as the response BODY TEXT ONLY -- it does not call .as_error() on the response, and neither to_call_tool_result()'s is_error field nor render_json()'s "isError" key are derived from this internal validate() outcome at all; both read only the builder's own is_error field, set exclusively via AgentResponse::as_error(), which toon_body()'s internal validate() failure never calls. So an invalid ToonOptions still renders with is_error: false / "isError":false -- indistinguishable at the is_error/isError level from a genuinely successful response, even though validate() itself was in fact called. This module does not rely on that internal call being sufficient: render_projection() (AC-004B) constructs a standalone ToonOptions and calls its validate() explicitly, and only ever constructs a michi::AgentResponse in the Ok branch of that check -- an AgentResponse is never built from a ToonOptions this module already knows to be invalid, so AgentResponse::toon_body()'s own internal validate() call (confirmed above to exist, but to only ever affect body text) is never reached with invalid input from this module in the first place. If render_projection()'s own explicit validate() call returns an Err, this module constructs a DomainError directly via a separate, standalone function -- toon_validation_error(e: &michi::toon::ToonError) -> DomainError, NOT the ToDomainError trait (which is implemented only for MonoklError, per AC-007's closed set of exactly 14 monokl_code() values; a ToonError is not a MonoklError variant and constructing one via ToDomainError would either require inventing a 15th monokl_code() value outside that closed set, or misusing an existing one for an unrelated failure -- neither is acceptable). toon_validation_error(e) constructs DomainError::new(ErrorCode::ExternalFailure, format!("toon_render_invalid: {e}")).retryable(false) directly, using the same "prefix: detail" message convention AC-007/AC-010 establish for MonoklError but scoped to this module's own internal-bug-shaped failure, not to any MonoklError variant -- since an invalid ToonOptions at this point indicates a bug in this module's own row/field construction (a ToonProjection<N> implementation producing a value validate() rejects), not a caller input error.

crates/monokl/Cargo.toml gains exactly one new optional dependency line: `michi = { git = "https://github.com/orin-dx/michi", rev = "cb355b8c05048e71e7219af8416c475346b6f837", optional = true, default-features = false, features = ["miette"] }`. (default-features = false is inconsequential here, not load-bearing: michi's own root Cargo.toml declares `default = []`, so there are no default features to opt out of -- it is included for explicitness and consistency with io-errors' own dependency line, not because omitting it would pull in anything.)
